actions.action: Check whether the soil is dry an inch down and the pot feels light
If the soil is wet but plants are limp, inspect stems at the soil line and roots for rot
Divide the root ball into 3–4 clumps, discard rotted stems, and pot each clump in its own 4–6 inch pot with drainage and potting mix
Water each pot thoroughly until it drains whenever the top inch is dry
Move the plants to the sunniest south- or west-facing window
Alternatively, set up a grow light 6–12 inches above the plants for 12–14 hours a day
Take 3–4 inch cuttings, strip the lower leaves and root them in a glass of water

reason: The answer leads with overcrowding and offers thirst only as one option alongside rot. A thorough soak is mentioned within a soil check, but the main fix is dividing and repotting, so the advice is only partial. Nothing in it is likely to harm the plant.
